name: Bengaluru network and traffic data sources
type: dataset survey (network geometry, signal timings, counts, speeds, congestion indices) for a Bengaluru traffic simulator
maintainer: Several: OpenStreetMap contributors (OSM Foundation, ODbL); OpenCity.in (Oorvani Foundation civic data portal, hosting documents from Bengaluru Traffic Police (BTP), BBMP/GBA, BDA, BMRCL, DULT); Bengaluru Traffic Police and C-DAC (B-ATCS adaptive signals); TomTom (Traffic Index, Traffic Stats); IISc CDPG/CiSTUP and AIM@IISc (Bengaluru Mobility Challenge, UVH-26 image dataset)
first_release: OSM Bengaluru mapping from the late 2000s [uncertain]; OpenCity BTP signal-timing and one-way datasets catalogued 2022-04-11; BBMP road-width map catalogued 2024-04-18; RITES Hebbal study dated 15 Dec 2021; B-ATCS launched Oct 2024; TomTom Traffic Index annual (2025 edition published Jan 2026)
last_activity: OSM: live (Overpass snapshot used here 2026-11-11T09:56Z; Geofabrik India extract contains data to 2026-11-09). OpenCity: Hebbal tunnel dataset updated 2026-10-11; GBA elevated-corridor datasets with KML updated 2026-10-14; BTP signal-timing set metadata touched 2025-11-27. TomTom Traffic Index 2025 released Jan 2026. Arcadis B-ATCS case study April 2026.
licence: OSM: ODbL 1.0 (attribution + share-alike on derived databases). OpenCity: most government documents labelled 'Other (Public Domain)'; the BTP signal-timing, BTP one-way and DULT CMP datasets carry no licence field in the CKAN metadata [uncertain]. TomTom Traffic Index: viewable web pages only, data proprietary; Traffic Stats is a paid commercial API with 30-day trial. Bengaluru Mobility Challenge data: restricted to approved competition participants. UVH-26: described by IISc as open-source licence [uncertain which].
code_availability: Data, not code. Downloadable today: OSM via Overpass API or Geofabrik southern-zone-latest.osm.pbf (533 MB); OpenCity CKAN API (package_show/package_search) returns direct PDF/CSV/KML URLs. Not downloadable: B-ATCS live signal state, BTP junction counts, TomTom segment speeds (commercial), Bengaluru Mobility Challenge videos (participants only).
maintenance_health: OSM Bengaluru is actively edited: new structures already present (Silkboard Double Decker Flyover ways, 'Ragigudda-Silk Board Integrated Flyover', a way still named '(u/c)', Hebbal ramp ways with OSM IDs above 1.42 billion, i.e. 2025-2026 edits). OpenCity is actively adding project DPRs (Hebbal tunnel, GBA elevated corridors with KML alignments in Oct 2026). BTP signal-timing PDFs are one-off scans of fixed-time plans (cycle 125-235 s) and predate B-ATCS adaptive control at about 169 junctions, so they are likely stale for B-ATCS junctions [uncertain].
mixed_traffic_support: Data side only: classified counts by mode exist only inside PDF reports, e.g. RITES Hebbal 2051 input of 33,765 veh/h = car 8,354, taxi 6,266, two-wheeler 11,835, auto 2,437, bus 1,044, LCV 1,392, truck 1,741, multi-axle 696 (41,596 PCU). No open machine-readable classified count dataset was found for Bengaluru.
non_lane_behaviour: No source gives lateral position or trajectory data for Bengaluru. OSM carries lanes but not effective usable width; the BBMP road-width KML gives right-of-way style widths (RR_WIDTH_P values such as 12, 18, 24, 30, 45 m) that could size a strip-based carriageway, but the field meaning is not documented [uncertain]. UVH-26 / BMD-45 CCTV image datasets could in principle feed detection, not trajectories.
seepage_filtering_support: N/A for data sources; none of the sources measures two-wheeler seepage. Must come from literature parameters.
per_class_parameters: Implied PCU factors from the RITES Hebbal table (PCU/vehicle): car 1.0, taxi 1.0, auto 1.0, two-wheeler 0.75, bus 3.0, LCV 2.0, truck 4.0, multi-axle 4.0. IIT-B Hebbal report says it used IRC PCU factors; critics say these are 1990s factors that may overstate two-wheeler impact by about 30%.
indian_calibration_evidence: Usable field numbers found: (1) RITES Hebbal VISSIM base 2019: 14 directional peak-hour volumes with GEH (e.g. City->Hebbal 7,946 observed vs 7,796 simulated, GEH 1.69; GEH < 10 for 85% of values) and 6 section speeds (16-29 km/h observed). (2) IIT-B Hebbal: junction peak-hour 32,770 veh (31,758 PCU) at Hebbal and 28,493 veh (27,863 PCU) at Mekhri Circle, 09:00-10:00; travel speeds 4.29, 3.57 and 8.3 km/h on surveyed routes. (3) TomTom 2025: 36 min 9 s per 10 km average, 74.4% congestion, morning peak 14.6 km/h, evening peak 13.2 km/h (BTP disputes, says about 34.5 min per 10 km at peak).
calibration_dataset_used: Best available open targets: RITES Hebbal 2019 peak-hour turning-movement diagram (26,896 PCU total, by approach) plus directional volumes and section speeds (PDF, public domain on OpenCity); IIT-B / tunnel DPR junction totals and speed-delay runs (PDF); BTP fixed-time signal plans for roughly 240 junctions in 124 PDFs (most PDFs cover a pair of junctions). None is machine-readable; numbers must be transcribed.
calibration_method: N/A for the data sources themselves (RITES used GEH on link volumes plus speed comparison; see C06).
validation_against_field_case: Hebbal is the only Bengaluru junction found with an open, numeric base-year calibration table (RITES 2019 VISSIM) plus a public BTP signal plan for the at-grade junction under the flyover. Silk Board has a BTP signal plan and only percentage before/after congestion figures.
network_import: OpenStreetMap is the only practical network source. Overpass check on 2026-11-11 of all motorway/trunk/primary/secondary/tertiary (+_link) ways in bbox 12.83,77.45,13.14,77.78 (15,288 ways, 3,996 km): length share with tag present - lanes 48% overall (motorway 97%, trunk 96%, primary 70%, secondary 47%, tertiary 28%, primary_link 33%); oneway tagged on 100% of trunk/motorway and 89% of primary (divided roads are drawn as two one-way carriageways); width only 1% (values mixed: '10', '12 m', "40'"); maxspeed 19% (trunk 70%); turn:lanes about 0%; lanes:forward about 0%. Bridges: 925 bridge ways (142.5 km), 880 carry layer (852 layer=1, 26 layer=2, 2 layer=3), 45 have no layer; 617 bridge ways on secondary-or-higher roads, 597 with layer but only 407 with lanes and 6 with width. 184 ways named '*Flyover*' (59 distinct names): all have layer, 133 have lanes. 55 major-road ways have layer>0 without a bridge tag and 39 have layer<0 without tunnel/covered. A node-sharing check found 0 bridge ways whose interior nodes are shared with a layer-0 ground road (no false at-grade connections). Corridor examples: Outer Ring Road (625 ways, 136 km): lanes 84%, oneway 99%, width 1%, layer 13%, maxspeed 77%. Hebbal (box 13.030-13.045 N, 77.585-77.600 E): 19 bridge ways all lanes+layer, e.g. way 377852248 'Hebbal Flyover' trunk lanes=3 layer=1 (468 m), way 379862163 'Flyover Ramp' lanes=2 layer=2, way 693773357 'Hebbal Flyover' lanes=1 width=3; but only 67% of all ways there have lanes. Silk Board: way 40696221/40696222 'Silk Board Flyover' trunk lanes=3 layer=1 (456 m each); way 886153772 'Ragigudda-Silk Board Integrated Flyover' primary lanes=2 bridge=viaduct layer=1 (2,079 m); way 1254771465 'Silk Board Interchange' lanes=2 layer=2; way 519734960 'Silkboard Double Decker Flyover' lanes=4 layer=1; the metro deck above is a separate railway layer. K R Puram/Tin Factory: way 172886625/172886626 'Tin Factory Flyover' trunk lanes=2 layer=1 (241 m each), way 380724513 'Benniganahalli Flyover' lanes=3 layer=1; only 62% of ways in the box have lanes and 69% oneway. Richmond Circle: 8 'Richmond Circle Flyover' ways all with layer=1 but 4 of 8 lack lanes (e.g. way 36852353, 346 m) and two say lanes=1. Goraguntepalya: way 380052398/380052400 'Goraguntepalya Flyover' motorway lanes=2 layer=1, about 4.4 km each.
demand_input_formats: No open OD matrix exists for any Bengaluru corridor (the IIT-B report says neither DPR contains an OD survey and treats diversion as an assumed 50-80%). Usable demand inputs are PDF tables: peak-hour turning movements by approach in PCU (RITES Hebbal), junction totals (IIT-B), classified mode volumes (RITES 2051). The DULT Comprehensive Mobility Plan 2020 PDF is the citywide zonal source [uncertain whether it publishes link counts]. Practical approach: hand-transcribe turning counts into a JSON flow file per approach and vehicle class.
data_access: 1) OSM: Overpass API (free, fair-use) for corridor clips; Geofabrik India southern-zone-latest.osm.pbf 533 MB (daily); licence ODbL. 2) OpenCity CKAN (data.opencity.in/api/3/action/...): 'bengaluru-city-traffic-signal-data' - 124 PDFs from BTP with fixed-time phase diagrams, phase splits and cycle times by time of day (e.g. Hebbal Fly Over junction Ring Road x Bellary Road: 4 phases, cycle 130 s off-peak and 160 s at 08:00-11:00 and 16:30-21:30; Marathahalli Bridge: cycle 155/225 s; Sarjapur Road Checkpost: cycle 175-235 s); 'bengaluru-one-way-roads' - CSV of 259 one-way roads (columns: sub-division, police station, road, from, to, notification number, date), text descriptions not geometry; 'bengaluru-road-width-map' - 25.7 MB KML, 23,238 placemarks with RR_WIDTH_P (most common 12, 6, 24, 18, 9, 45, 15, 30 m) and RR_width_B (about half of P), likely Revised Master Plan road widths, field meaning [uncertain]; Hebbal tunnel dataset (DPR, IIT-B microsimulation report, IISc review); RITES Hebbal capacity report (BMRCL); GBA elevated-corridor datasets with KML alignments; BTP violations/crash CSVs; BTP jurisdiction KML. 3) B-ATCS: about 169 junctions (Phase I: 155 upgraded + 14 new) on C-DAC CoSiCoSt adaptive logic; no public data feed or API found. 4) TomTom: Traffic Index 2025 city-level figures on the web page; segment speeds only via paid Traffic Stats (30-day API trial, 60-day batch evaluation). 5) Bengaluru Mobility Challenge 2024 (IEEE DataPort DOI 10.21227/8ey0-sw97): videos from 23 Safe City cameras in north Bengaluru, restricted to participants, users reported download failures. 6) UVH-26 (26,646 CCTV images) and BMD-45 on Hugging Face: images for detection, no counts.
reuse_mode: Use as data. OSM -> network geometry, lanes, oneway, layer (pre-import offline). BTP signal PDFs -> hand-coded fixed-time plans for the demo junctions. RITES/IIT-B tables -> demand and validation targets. BBMP width KML -> optional carriageway-width hint. TomTom -> only a city-level sanity check, not an input.
effort_within_72_hours: Feasible in about 4-6 hours for one corridor: Overpass clip (minutes), manual lane/width patching of about 10-30 ways (1-2 h), transcribing one BTP signal sheet and one turning-movement diagram (1-2 h), checking layer/connectivity (1 h). Cut: citywide import, BBMP width conflation (spatial matching of a 25 MB KML is a day's work), any attempt to get B-ATCS or TomTom data, and classified demand beyond the RITES mix.
licence_constraint: Shipping an OSM-derived network JSON to browsers is public conveyance of a derivative database: it must be offered under ODbL with '(c) OpenStreetMap contributors' attribution and a link to openstreetmap.org/copyright. Mixing in BTP signal timings and RITES counts (public-domain or unlicensed government documents) is fine; keep them as separate layers/files so they are not pulled into share-alike [uncertain how OSMF would classify a merged file]. Do not use TomTom data in a shipped product without a commercial licence.
known_limitations: OSM: width almost never tagged (1%); lanes missing on about half of all major-road length and on a third of bridge ways; turn:lanes essentially absent, so lane-to-lane connectivity at junctions must be guessed; service roads beside flyovers are often unlaned; some bridges have no layer (45) and some layered ways have no bridge tag (55); a few ways under construction are already in the data. OpenCity: almost everything is PDF or scanned drawing, so numbers need manual transcription; signal plans are fixed-time and undated and likely superseded at B-ATCS junctions; one-way list has no geometry; the width KML field meanings are undocumented. Counts: no open, machine-readable traffic counts or OD for Bengaluru; DPR counts predate structural changes (Hebbal ramp opened Jan 2026). TomTom: city aggregates only; BTP publicly disputes its numbers by about 10%.
documented_failures: IIT-B Hebbal study built its base model on DPR counts without OD data or real signal timings ('junction control is represented on an assumed basis'), and the IISc review found its base speed (13.74 km/h) inconsistent with the 4.29 km/h observed in the DPR; experts also noted the data predates the January 2026 Hebbal ramp. The Bengaluru Mobility Challenge dataset was announced as open to participants but many could not download it. The BTP signal-timing PDFs embed timings in drawings, so automated extraction is unreliable (pdftotext output interleaves diagram labels).
validation_approach: Direct inspection: Overpass API queries on 2026-11-11 with length-weighted tag-completeness statistics computed per highway class and per corridor box, plus a node-sharing check between bridge ways and layer-0 roads; OpenCity CKAN API listing of datasets, licences and resource formats; download and text extraction of the BTP signal PDFs (Hebbal, Silk Board/Checkpost, Marathahalli), the one-way CSV and the road-width KML attribute schema.
takeaway_for_our_build: Treat OSM as the geometry and topology source but never as the source of truth for capacity: (1) pre-import the corridor offline from Overpass, keep the OSM way IDs, and ship a small hand-reviewed patch file that sets lanes and carriageway width for every link the demo uses (default lanes by class when absent: trunk 3, primary 2, link roads 1-2; default lane width 3.0-3.5 m, matching the 3.0 m at-grade / 3.5 m elevated values quoted in the Hebbal DPR). (2) Derive z-level from layer, falling back to layer=1 for bridge without layer and -1 for tunnel; flag layer-without-bridge for review. (3) Encode the BTP fixed-time plan for the junction under the flyover as the default signal program and let the user edit it. (4) Use RITES Hebbal 2019 turning PCUs and GEH table as the single validation target. (5) Put OSM attribution and the ODbL link in the UI and in the shipped network file.
